matches.rationale: Ground truth 1 concerns the abstract's claim of 14.6% improvement lacking statistical variability or confidence intervals. None of the findings address this specific issue in the abstract; pred_id 1 discusses Table 5 ablation inconsistencies, not the abstract's claims.
Ground truth 2 identifies a fabricated historical reference 'Filippini, 1892' in the Introduction. None of the findings mention this reference or any fabricated citation issue in the Introduction.

Ground truth 3 concerns inconsistency in how action embeddings (computed as state differences in Section 3.2) integrate with the model's loss and prediction heads described in Sections 3.1 and 3.3. None of the findings address this methodological inconsistency.

Ground truth 4 identifies missing hyperparameter tuning details for baselines in the Experiments section, potentially causing unfair comparisons. None of the findings discuss hyperparameter tuning or baseline optimization protocols.

Ground truth 5 concerns Table 1 presenting point estimates without variance or confidence intervals. While pred_id 1 discusses Table 1, it focuses on numerical inconsistencies with Table 5, not the absence of statistical variability measures.
Ground truth 6 identifies missing ethical considerations and bias discussion in the Conclusion. None of the findings address ethical integrity omissions or responsible AI deployment concerns.

Ground truth 7 concerns contradiction between Section 3.1 claiming ground-truth labels on all frames and Section 3.2 stating frame-level annotations are absent (using pseudo labels). None of the findings identify this cross-section inconsistency about supervision granularity.

Ground truth 8 identifies rhetorical inflation in the Introduction using terms like 'powerful' and 'promising pathway' without tempering expectations. None of the findings address rhetorical presentation issues.

Ground truth 9 concerns Table 4 showing suspiciously minimal performance changes when increasing graph concepts from 5 to 15. None of the findings discuss Table 4 or this specific data integrity issue.

Ground truth 10 identifies ambiguity in Section 4.1 and Tables 1-2 about privileged information usage during evaluation. While pred_id 1 mentions Table 1, it does not address the privileged information protocol issue.

Ground truth 11 concerns suspicious training time discrepancies in Section 4.1 (8 hours for ChangeIt vs. 30 minutes for HowToChange despite similar dataset sizes). None of the findings address training time inconsistencies.
Ground truth 12 identifies missing criteria for VLM-based frame filtering in Section 3.1. None of the findings discuss this methodological ambiguity about background frame filtering.

Ground truth 13 concerns overstated generalization claims in the Experiments section about multi-action scenarios that were never tested. None of the findings address this claim-evidence mismatch regarding multi-action generalization.

Ground truth 14 identifies rhetorical exaggeration in the Conclusion about integrating SAGE into vision foundation models. None of the findings address rhetorical presentation issues in the Conclusion.

Ground truth 15 concerns Table 2(b) showing extreme baseline degradation on novel objects/actions without explanation, suggesting selective reporting. None of the findings discuss Table 2(b) or this specific data integrity issue.
